planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall into humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Saxifraga umbrosa forms tidy evergreen rosettes of leathery, spoon-shaped, scalloped leaves that knit together into a low, weed-suppressing mat over time. In late spring, wiry flower stems rise above the foliage carrying loose, airy sprays of small, star-shaped white to pale pink flowers flecked with deeper spots. It is one of the wild parent species of the better-known hybrid London Pride (Saxifraga x urbium) but stays somewhat smaller and more compact in the garden. Grow it in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade, where established clumps tolerate root competition and brief dry spells better than many woodland groundcovers.
